challenges.title: Name the blocker
challenges.challenge: On a sticky note, write one goal and the one habit that's blocking it. Be specific. Put it on your bathroom mirror.
challenges.why: Change starts with an honest look at where you are, kept where you can't avoid it.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: one move against that habit before you open your phone.

challenges.title: Before the phone
challenges.challenge: Read your mirror note out loud this morning. Take one small action against that habit before you open your phone.
challenges.why: A goal you face every morning is harder to dodge than one you keep in your head.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: three honest notes on the mirror. Facts, not insults.

challenges.title: Three honest notes
challenges.challenge: Add three notes to your mirror: one thing you keep avoiding, one excuse you lean on, and one task you'll finish this week. Keep them factual.
challenges.why: Plain truth, said without insults, is something you can act on.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: find the weakest part of one skill and work on just that.

challenges.title: Find the weak spot
challenges.challenge: Pick one skill your goal depends on. Name the exact part where you're weakest, then spend 10 minutes working only on that part.
challenges.why: Improvement starts with a precise diagnosis, not a general wish to be better.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: list five hard things you've already come through.

challenges.title: Fill the jar
challenges.challenge: Write down five hard things you've already come through, big or small. Save the list somewhere you can open it in seconds.
challenges.why: Proof of what you've handled before is the best answer to doubt today.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: log your whole day in 30-minute blocks. No changes yet.

challenges.title: Log the day
challenges.challenge: Today, note what you actually do in 30-minute blocks from waking to bed. Don't fix anything yet. Just record it honestly.
challenges.why: You can't take back time you haven't measured.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: take back one wasted half hour and give it to your goal.

challenges.title: Take back time
challenges.challenge: From yesterday's log, pick one 30-minute block that didn't serve you. Use 15 minutes of it today for your mirror goal.
challenges.why: Most people don't lack time. They lack a plan for it. Raise the standard.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: do the task you've put off longest, before anything else.

challenges.title: Hard thing first
challenges.challenge: Pick the small task you've been putting off longest. Do it first today, before anything easier gets your attention.
challenges.why: Small, regular doses of discomfort build a mind that doesn't flinch.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: when you want to stop, go a little further first.

challenges.title: A little further
challenges.challenge: In a workout or focused task today, when you first want to stop, add a little more: a few good-form reps or five more minutes. Stop at any sharp pain.
challenges.why: The first urge to quit is a signal, not your limit.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: win the one second where quitting happens.

challenges.title: Win the second
challenges.challenge: The next time you feel the pull to skip or give up today, pause. Take three slow breaths, picture what happens if you fold, then choose.
challenges.why: Most quitting happens in one moment. Be ready for that moment.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: one line on why your hardest task matters.

challenges.title: Write the why
challenges.challenge: Before your hardest task today, write one sentence on why it matters to you. Read it again when the task gets uncomfortable.
challenges.why: A reason decided in advance holds up better than one you look for under pressure.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: two everyday tasks with your other hand.

challenges.title: Other hand day
challenges.challenge: Do two everyday tasks with your non-dominant hand, like brushing your teeth or stirring your coffee. When it feels clumsy, keep going.
challenges.why: Choosing to be awkward on purpose is how a weak side gets stronger.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: rehearse your hardest moment before it arrives.

challenges.title: Rehearse the obstacle
challenges.challenge: Spend five minutes picturing tomorrow's hardest moment. See where it could go wrong, and decide now what you'll do if it does.
challenges.why: When you've already met the obstacle in your head, it can't catch you off guard.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: do one small thing you've been avoiding out of fear.

challenges.title: Walk toward it
challenges.challenge: Pick one small thing you've avoided out of fear: a call, a question, a hard conversation. Do it today, even if it feels awkward.
challenges.why: Fear shrinks when you move toward it and grows when you hide. Raise the standard.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: plan an earlier start and protect the extra half hour.

challenges.title: Start earlier
challenges.challenge: Tonight, set your alarm 30 minutes earlier and go to bed 30 minutes earlier too. Decide now what you'll do with that first half hour.
challenges.why: An earlier start buys time before the day's demands find you.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: watch someone excellent and ask why it works.

challenges.title: Study the tape
challenges.challenge: Watch 10 minutes of someone excellent in your field: a talk, a match, a demo. Pause often, ask why each move works, and note one to try.
challenges.why: Watch to learn how it works, not just to enjoy it.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: replay one of your own moments and find two better options.

challenges.title: Replay your moment
challenges.challenge: Pick one moment this week that didn't go well. Write down two other ways you could have handled it, and circle the one you'll use next time.
challenges.why: Looking at what could have happened sharpens what you'll do next.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: ask one real question of someone further ahead.

challenges.title: Ask further ahead
challenges.challenge: Send one specific question to someone further ahead than you in your field. Make it a real question you want answered, not small talk.
challenges.why: Asking feels awkward for a minute. Not asking can cost you months.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: read the actual rules of something you compete in.

challenges.title: Read the rules
challenges.challenge: Read the actual rules of something you compete in: a policy at work, a contract, the rules of your sport. Note one detail most people miss.
challenges.why: Knowing the rules better than others is preparation few people bother with.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: 15 minutes of work no one will ever see.

challenges.title: Unseen work
challenges.challenge: Do 15 minutes of work on your goal that no one will see or praise. Don't post it and don't mention it.
challenges.why: The results people notice rest on work they never see.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: arrive early and sit in five minutes of quiet.

challenges.title: Arrive early, settle
challenges.challenge: Get to your most important meeting, session or task five minutes early. Sit quietly without your phone and settle before it starts.
challenges.why: Calm you build before the noise is calm you can carry into it.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: 10 slow, correct minutes on your most basic skill.

challenges.title: Basics, done right
challenges.challenge: Spend 10 minutes on the most basic skill in your work or sport. Do it slowly and correctly, with no shortcuts and nothing fancy.
challenges.why: Solid basics put you ahead of the many people who skip them.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: do one dull job to a standard you'd be proud of.

challenges.title: Pride in small jobs
challenges.challenge: Pick one dull task today, like the dishes, an email or a report. Do it to your best standard, as if someone you respect will check it.
challenges.why: Standards are built in the jobs nobody notices.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: an honest after-action report on one recent miss.

challenges.title: After-action report
challenges.challenge: Pick one recent failure. Write what went well, what went wrong and one fix. Put the fix in your calendar.
challenges.why: A miss you study honestly becomes a plan for next time.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: do your work at the usual time, whatever yesterday brought.

challenges.title: Same time, any result
challenges.challenge: Whatever happened yesterday, good or bad, work on your goal at your usual time today. Don't let the result move the routine.
challenges.why: A routine that doesn't depend on results is one you can trust.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: set a goal you fully control, not an outcome.

challenges.title: Control the process
challenges.challenge: Write one goal for today that's an action you fully control, not a result. Say "make five calls", not "close a deal". Then do it.
challenges.why: Results follow the process, so put your attention where your control is.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: write your own one-line code and put it on the mirror.

challenges.title: Write your code
challenges.challenge: Write a one- or two-line personal code: what you stand for and the standard you hold yourself to. Put it on the mirror beside your goal.
challenges.why: Your own principles keep you steady when nobody else is giving direction.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: look at who's in your corner and tell one of them your goal.

challenges.title: Check your corner
challenges.challenge: Think of the three people you spend the most time with. Pick the one who pushes you forward and tell them what you're working on.
challenges.why: The people closest to you either help carry your goals or make them heavier.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: help one person who's a step behind you.

challenges.title: Bring someone along
challenges.challenge: Help one person who's a step behind you today: share a tip, review their work, or walk them through something you know well.
challenges.why: Getting ahead counts for more when you bring others with you.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: mark one win, then set the next goal and start again.

challenges.title: Start again at zero
challenges.challenge: Look back over your 30 days and write down one win. Then set your next goal on the mirror and treat tomorrow as day one.
challenges.why: Mark the win, then reset. The next level starts from zero. Raise the standard.
challenges.tomorrow_teaser: Tomorrow: a new block starts. Same mirror, higher standard.
